reason: Selected controlled misinformation results support skepticism prompts and exposure-matched baselines, while showing a late verifier can fail.

candidates.title: Test a source-unreliability warning before adding a verifier agent
candidates.rule: When agents reason from potentially false retrieved or peer-produced context, compare a short source-skepticism instruction with the existing prompt before adding a late verification agent.
candidates.passage: A verifier agent that speaks before the vote does not help.
candidates.finding: At full misinformation exposure the warning improves eight of nine model-task cells with confidence intervals excluding zero, up to 0.18 under voting. True/no-context changes have intervals including zero. The tested late verifier never improves accuracy and hurts two ethics cells.
candidates.conditions: Three-agent homogeneous debates using judge-filtered machine-written misinformation. Warning enters the discussion prompt; verifier arrives after agents state their solutions.
candidates.limitations: No significant observed true-context cost is not proof of zero cost. Results need human-written sources and heterogeneous teams; the verifier result concerns one timing and design, not all verification.
candidates.validation_test: Compare no warning, skepticism and a verifier under false, true and absent context with matched exposure; report accuracy, source adoption and token cost.

candidates.title: Match misinformation exposure when evaluating debate
candidates.rule: When evaluating whether debate resists misleading context, compare independent voting with the same number of informed and misinformed samples, rather than only a fully exposed single agent.
candidates.passage: Uninformed majorities win by outvoting, not by convincing.
candidates.finding: With an uninformed majority, apparent robustness largely comes from dilution; with a misinformed majority, interaction can recover accuracy. The recommendation is an evaluation rule inferred from these decompositions, not a method for knowing which agents are wrong in deployment.
workloads: MINT three- and five-agent debate experiments
candidates.conditions: Control passage relevance, exposed-agent count, speaking order and decision protocol.
candidates.limitations: Machine-generated and judge-selected misinformation; fixed speaking order and homogeneous groups. Debate consumes substantially more tokens than independent voting, so exposure matching alone is not cost matching.
candidates.validation_test: Sweep exposed-agent fraction and order; compare independent votes and debate under identical exposure and separate matched-cost tests. Keep true-context controls.

review_scope: Selected abstract, introduction, methods or main-result sections; not a comprehensive paper or appendix review.
